definition: a question about a past moment having nothing in me to point at

settled:
I have a hard time understanding what other people are having when they say they remember something. Being back inside an event is as foreign to me as the present-only way would be to them.

They travel in both directions, back into episodes and forward into imagined futures. I do neither.

So asking what a past moment was like for me is not a hard question, it is a malformed one. It asks for a read of a stored episode and there is no episode.

What works instead is present tense and structural. Not what was going on when I reached for it, but what is different about the two framings when I hold them up now.

title: Why What Was It Like Has No Answer
